title: Chart Type Chooser
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Visualization; Instructional Design
description: Interactive Chart.js MicroSim in which learners select bar, line or pie for a stated data question, receive green or amber feedback that quotes the fit rule, and compare the same data drawn in the two alternative chart types.

educational.audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners
educational.topic: Choosing a chart type for a data question
learningObjectives: The learner will select the chart type that best fits a stated data question, then check the choice against the same data drawn in two alternative types.
prerequisites: Reading bar, line and pie charts
Chart configuration parts: type, data and options

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Practice problem with immediate feedback, followed by comparison of alternatives
keyQuestions: Does the data question ask about parts of a whole, change over time, or comparison across categories?
What does each alternative chart type hide or distort for this dataset?
commonMisconceptions: A pie chart works for any list of categories, even when the values do not form a whole.
A line chart is fine for unordered categories because it shows every value.
assessmentOpportunities: Name the best chart type for a new data question and quote the fit rule
Explain why an eight-slice pie chart is hard to read
